conditional_findings.first_contract: A represented physical floor outline must have a topology compatible with its later convex fan, or its supported projection domain and consumer policy must explicitly account for rounding-induced inversions.
conditional_findings.classification: New current source assessment; no historical unique-count increment. A deliberate small-bend policy exists and is preserved.
conditional_findings.trace: Take the strictly convex counterclockwise points A=(0,0), B=(4,0), C=(4,2), D=(161/64,81/64). All coordinates are exactly representable binary32. Their consecutive exact cross products are 8, 95/32, 1/32 and 81/16, so the shown ordered PlanPolygon constructor accepts the finite, distinct, positive-area shape under its arithmetic. A finite translation by (2^23,2^23) is accepted as PlanDisplacement. Under ordinary round-to-nearest binary32 addition, subtracting the common translation from the represented result gives A=(0,0), B=(4,0), C=(4,2), D=(3,1): the two fractional components of D round to3 and1. The resulting double signed area is6, all vertices remain distinct, and the C→D→A turn is −2, so from_rigid_projection admits a represented concave outline. No constructor, translation, floating operation or product was executed; this is exact dyadic/rounding reasoning from the pinned source.
conditional_findings.consumer_and_safeguards: FloorRegion::from_scene rechecks the exact convex constructor and would reject these translated vertices; do not claim that path accepts them. FloorRegion::from_architectural retains the original convex source and reconstructs the rounded projection without the exact recheck. Under the explicit assumption that the selected native sin_cos(0) returns the identity, an architectural polygon with these coordinates, zero origin, identity orientation and centre (2^23,2^23) has the same represented outline. The selected single-building recipe path creates that kind of region; if a complete valid recipe, placement, floor request and all intervening checks reach convex_floor, its fan contains triangles A-B-C and A-C-D. The second lies inside the first and has opposite signed orientation, so the geometric fan covers the concavity rather than exactly the polygon. Source test rounded_architectural_edges_keep_union_coverage_without_masking_missing_faces documents an intentional small rounded-bend use case; its assertions were not executed. The much larger 2^23m position, actual recipe shape, sin_cos backend, whole-scene support, admission/coverage guards, native triangle winding and user impact are unproved. Ordinary city generation may constrain positions and has not been shown to produce this input.
